ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are upper and lower main structural fragments, and several curved arrows are included; according to the problem, the curved arrows are not counted in the number of bonds. The upper fragment is a six-membered ring, with a nitrogen atom on the right side of the ring, the nitrogen atom is connected to a methyl group, and a C=C double bond is drawn in the ring. The lower fragment is an anhydride/carbonyl system containing two CF3 substituents: on the left and right there is each one CF3 connected to a carbonyl carbon, in the middle there is an oxygen atom connecting two carbonyl carbons, and there are two C=O double bonds. Reasoning count: Exclude all bonds involving hydrogen. In the upper fragment, the six-membered ring itself has 6 ring bonds, among which the drawn C=C is counted as one double bond; plus one bond of N-CH3, totaling 7. In the lower fragment, the left CF3 has 3 C-F bonds, plus 1 C-C bond from the CF3 carbon to the carbonyl carbon, totaling 4; the right CF3 is likewise 4; the two C=O double bonds count as 2; the two C-O single bonds between the central oxygen and the two carbonyl carbons count as 2. The lower total is 4 + 4 + 2 + 2 = 12. The total is 7 + 12 = 19.

method.method_draft: First describe the visible structure, then count by parts. For the upper component, count the six ring bonds, including the drawn C=C as one double bond, and add the N-CH3 bond, giving 7. For the lower component, count the left CF3 group as three C-F bonds plus the C-C bond to the carbonyl carbon, the right CF3 group similarly as three C-F bonds plus its C-C bond, the two C=O bonds, and the two single bonds through the central oxygen between the two carbonyl carbons. This gives 12 for the lower fragment. Add the two component totals, 7 + 12, to get 19.
